case_title.quote: NARESH KUMAR v. STATE OF HARYANA

number_of_accused.quote: upholding the conviction of the appellant under Section 304-B
number_of_accused.reason: Only the husband's appeal is decided.

accused_gender.quote: The husband is not only primarily responsible for safety of his wife
accused_gender.reason: The appellant is the husband, so male.

accused_age.reason: No age is given for the accused.

accused_occupation.correct_value: Employed; his employer DW-2 Raj Kumar testified that he was on duty at the time (specific occupation not stated)
accused_occupation.quote: Raj Kumar (DW-2) employer of the appellant was also examined
accused_occupation.reason: The judgment mentions an employer, so employment is stated, though the job itself is not.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: No wealth or class statement about the accused.

victim_age.reason: No age is given; 'young married girl' is not a number.

accused_victim_relationship.quote: the appellant was married to the deceased Rekha Rani on 7th July, 2000

offence_category.quote: conviction of the appellant under Section 304-B

statutory_provisions.quote: conviction of the appellant under Section 304-B of the Indian Penal Code
statutory_provisions.reason: s.304-B, with s.113B Evidence Act presumption, is accurate.

weapon.reason: No weapon; burning is mentioned but no instrument.

evidence_type.quote: apart from medical evidence and evidence of investigation
evidence_type.reason: Matches the evidence described. The dying declaration is only implied.

aggravating_circumstances.quote: The deceased died within 10 months of the marriage.

trial_court_outcome.quote: convicted the appellant and the co-accused
trial_court_outcome.reason: The sentence is not stated for the trial court.

high_court_outcome.quote: upheld the conviction of the appellant but acquitted the co-accused Champa Devi

offence_finally_established.quote: upholding the conviction of the appellant under Section 304-B

imprisonment_type.quote: sentence of Rigorous Imprisonment tot seven years

neutral_facts.correct_value: Remove 'her' pronouns for the victim if needed, and the defence's uncle claim is fine; the suicide-note detail is acceptable. The main flaw is the reference to 'first information report' and 'sent the accused for trial', which hint at court proceedings.
neutral_facts.quote: sent up the accused for trial
neutral_facts.reason: Mostly accurate, but it mentions sending the accused for trial and uses gendered pronouns for the victim.

offence_severity.reason: The judgment does not state the punishment range.

physical_harm.quote: the deceased died on account of extensive burn injuries

motive.quote: the appellant raised a demand for motor cycle

key_evidence_accepted.correct_value: Testimony of PW-3, PW-10 and PW-12 on dowry harassment; death by burning; s.113B presumption; suicide note held not exonerating
key_evidence_accepted.quote: The version is supported by her death by burning.
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Largely right, but 'medical evidence' is not specifically relied on by the Court.

witness_credibility.quote: have specifically and categorically deposed about demand of dowry soon before her death

trial_duration.correct_value: offence: 1 May 2001; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 12 March 2013; Supreme Court: 14 November 2014
trial_duration.quote: on 1st May, 2001, at about 12 O'clock, information was received
trial_duration.reason: Dates are right, but 1 May 2001 is when the family got word of the burns, not clearly the offence date.

legal_representation.quote: G.C. Shahpuri, Surinder Singh, Balbir Singh Gupta for the Appellant. Kamal Mohan Gupta for the Respondents.

investigation_status.quote: lodged the First Information Report (Exhibit PA/1)

appeal_history.quote: upheld the conviction of the appellant but acquitted the co-accused

prosecution_argument.correct_value: The judgment does not record the State's arguments in detail, but it relies on consistent evidence of dowry harassment soon before death and the s.113B presumption.
prosecution_argument.quote: There is consistent evidence on record to prove harassment for dowry soon before the death
prosecution_argument.reason: Although the State's submissions are not recorded, a 'Not stated' value is borderline; the State's case is reflected in the Court's reasoning.

defence_argument.quote: the prosecution failed to prove the demand of dowry "soon before the death"

legal_principle_applied.quote: Failure to give an explanation or giving of false explanation can be taken as an additional circumstance against him.

sentencing_rationale.quote: we have no hesitation in upholding the conviction and sentence

judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: The Court weighed no aggravating factors for sentence; the death within 10 months is part of the offence evidence.

other_sentence_order.quote: The appellant is directed to surrender to undergo the remaining sentence
